findings.claim: A CRLB or small local fit residual is not enough to establish a useful early-acquisition error rate. Rife and Boorstyn describe rare low-SNR global-maximum outliers: ordinary errors can approach the bound while occasional large errors dominate total MSE below threshold.
findings.support_locator: Paper excerpt pp. 593-596, especially explanation around pp. 595-596 that a distorted periodogram can place its global maximum far from the true tone and outliers then dominate MSE.
findings.decision_implication: Report tail/outlier probability, absolute-error quantiles, and time-to-first-qualified-estimate alongside RMSE and any model-based uncertainty. Keep the false-presence control separate from the frequency-accuracy metric.
findings.assumptions: Single tone with unknown phase and independent Gaussian noise in the paper's setup.
findings.applicability_gap: The paper's finite-record simulation conditions do not establish rates for this receiver, its reference-level units, payload activity, or proposed 6-second criterion.
findings.next_discriminator: At matched offsets and levels, count estimates outside 0.10 Hz and large acquisition outliers, not just within-lock residuals; include silence and payload/auxiliary-only controls.

findings.claim: For a clean stationary single complex sinusoid in white Gaussian noise, a low-cost estimator in Kay's family can approach the maximum-likelihood estimator's performance at moderately high SNR; the paper also explains why linear prediction does not attain the bound even at high SNR.
findings.support_locator: URI institutional record abstract, lines 28-29; citation and IEEE journal venue at lines 31-45.
findings.decision_implication: A small matched comparison of the existing estimator, a Kay-style frequency estimate, and a bounded fine-grid sinusoidal least-squares/profile-likelihood fit can determine whether an estimator limitation or acquisition/coherence conditions are dominant.
findings.assumptions: Single complex sinusoid, white Gaussian noise, and moderate-or-higher SNR; paper abstract does not expose enough detail to transfer exact implementation or confidence intervals.
findings.applicability_gap: Real capture is not established as a stationary complex AWGN tone; real-signal sideband/image ambiguity, ramps, interference, and changing amplitude may dominate.
findings.next_discriminator: Compare estimates on identical clean held-out PCM with randomized start phase; then add the known envelope/payload cases without changing estimator settings.

findings.claim: Differential-phase frequency estimation has a tunable lag: the generalized Kay paper reports lower variance than delay-one Kay at low SNR for its complex-AWGN model, while larger lags trade behavior and frequency range, so one lag is not universally best.
findings.support_locator: IEEE indexed abstract for 2006 paper: arbitrary-delay differential-phase ML derivation; delay-two high-SNR bound result; comparisons across range and SNR.
findings.decision_implication: If the current estimator relies on phase differences, a targeted lag sweep is a cheap discriminator, provided the phase remains coherent over the chosen lag and ambiguity is guarded.
findings.assumptions: Single complex sinusoid in complex AWGN; estimates are conditional on coherent observations.
findings.applicability_gap: The open publisher page failed, leaving only indexed abstract; native retuning with unknown per-hop phase invalidates cross-hop coherent lag assumptions. This literature does not validate the code's uncertainty field.
findings.next_discriminator: For one unretuned pilot burst, compare delay-one and a small bounded set of longer lags by error tails and lock range; separately invalidate coherence at retunes and chunk boundaries as applicable.

findings.claim: An estimator explicitly designed for lower SNR may be worth a control: Kay's 1984 article abstract reports a simple estimator with lower-SNR accuracy than then-current techniques, but the accessible abstract is too thin to rank it against current options.
findings.support_locator: URI institutional record abstract, lines 28-30; IEEE journal citation at lines 31-45.
findings.decision_implication: Treat it as a candidate baseline only if its assumptions and implementation can be reconstructed from the full paper; do not infer that it will beat the current estimator at the stated levels.
findings.assumptions: Sinusoids in white noise; convergence result for single sinusoid and simulation for multiple sinusoids.
findings.applicability_gap: Only abstract and citation were available; no algorithm details or quantified operating region were verified.
findings.next_discriminator: Retrieve full article through normal authorized library access if this candidate materially affects the decision; otherwise deprioritize it behind directly implementable alternatives.

findings.claim: The excerpts distinguish conditional frequency uncertainty from calibrated confidence: tracker intervals are engineering noise/variance gates; abrupt changes can exceed them before withdrawal. Optional long-profile frequency analysis separately tests recent presence and grants no phase/payload authority.
findings.support_locator: Supplied H03 lines 62-88 and 161-168; H05 lines 123-130 and 194-213. Supplied source facts; not runtime-tested.
findings.decision_implication: Validation should score both error coverage and admission timing, and must preserve uncertainty/provenance and frequency-only authority. Separate current presence qualification from accuracy on tone-present windows.
findings.applicability_gap: No code, runtime, or test execution was permitted in this case; the source excerpts establish neither actual measured behavior nor completeness.
findings.next_discriminator: Use a prospective matched capture matrix: offsets ±3/±12 Hz, both reference levels, clean/noisy and payload/auxiliary activity, plus 137- versus 4096-sample chunk delivery of identical samples. Measure chunk-invariant output timing, error quantiles, calibration/coverage, false admissions, and decline behavior.

rejected_or_redundant: Repeated tuning of the incumbent estimator is not yet justified: the literature indicates threshold/outlier behavior and model mismatch can masquerade as estimator variance; first separate stationary clean-tone accuracy from interference, coherence, and detection failures.
A finite uncertainty value or CRLB comparison alone cannot certify the proposed 95%/0.10-Hz target; these are planning numbers, and the opened sources do not validate them.
No estimator is shown superior. A matched discriminator with outlier and presence metrics should come first.
unresolved: The paper full texts for Kay 1989, Kay 1984, and IEEE 2006 were not accessed; exact estimator equations and their full operating regions remain unverified.

The Rife-Boorstyn IEEE page was blocked, so peer-review status was not independently verified from publisher or author-institutional evidence; publication in the cited IEEE journal is supported by bibliographic records, but review status is reported as unconfirmed.

No material here determines feasibility of 0.10 Hz by 6 seconds at 24/30 dB-Hz under the stated real capture geometry. Reference-level definition, actual noise spectrum/interferers, envelope duty cycle, and unannounced frequency evolution need operational clarification/measurement.
H03/H05/H06 are excerpts only; no runtime claims are made.

Web use: 13 logical operations (8 queries, 5 opens), including 3 failed opens; no simulations or project tests run.
escalation_ready: Sol/Astra can decide whether to authorize a small matched estimator/acquisition comparison: baseline versus one Kay-family candidate and bounded sinusoidal profile fit on identical captures, stratifying clean AWGN-like pilot, real envelope/payload, and absent-tone controls. Primary acceptance metrics should include time-to-first-valid estimate, tail error/outlier rate at <=0.10 Hz, false publications, uncertainty calibration/coverage, and chunking invariance. Literature is supportive of comparing approaches but supplies no architecture selection or target-feasibility proof.
